Triage: leveled finding → `pm:queue` / `domain:ui` / Task. Rationale: the docblock's "ONE reason" deletability test is load-bearing and false for `parentField` — that member's real keep-reason is the configPin operand, not JSDoc — and the cost already fired once (#6547's wrong assertion about where the renderer prose lives), so this grades queue over close. The fix is a two-line doc edit: state both reasons (documentation AND pin operand) so the deletability test reads right, and either give `parentField` its one-liner or note its pin-only status. Dispatch note: PR #6561 is writing standalone `parentField` prose in `@object-ui/types` — land this after it, on the merged ref; folding into another small plugin-gantt doc card is the ui seat's call. Size: S, mechanical.

Claim: PM session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q` (`domain:ui` execution seat, objectui). Branch `claude/issue-6563-ganttconfigrestated-rationale`. Dispatched this round to one `os-dev` agent, in its own worktree.

Picked as a Task rather than a Bug for a reason worth stating, since this lane's standing order is Bugs first: the Bug tier has **2** cards left and neither is dispatchable — #6457 lands in `packages/plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx`, serialized on #6458's active claim, and #6424 has just been marked `pm:retriage` because both of its dispositions sit on the human floor. The order says an exhausted tier falls back to Tasks rather than idling a slot, so it does.

**Why this card is worth an agent even though it changes no behaviour.** The docblock says the restated members are kept for *"ONE reason — their JSDoc"*, and `parentField` has no JSDoc. Its actual reason for existing is stated further down the same docblock: it is a **pin operand** for `ObjectGantt.configPin.test.ts`, giving that pin two independent halves so a spec bump that re-types one breaks the build. So a reader applying the "ONE reason" test literally would conclude `parentField` is deletable — and deleting it would silently remove a pin operand. That is a comment that makes a gate quietly deletable, which is worth more than its size suggests.

There is already a recorded cost: #6547 asserted, on the strength of this docblock, that the renderer prose for the spec-sourced keys lives in this type. For three of the four keys it turned out to be about, it did not.

⛔ Out of scope, stated to the agent: **deleting any `GanttConfigRestated` member** (that is the outcome this card exists to prevent, not to perform), and any change to `ObjectGantt.configPin.test.ts`'s operands. The agent is also told to **verify the pin claim** against the test rather than trust this card for it — if `parentField` turns out not to be an operand, the whole framing changes and that is a stop-and-report.

Hot-file note: `packages/plugin-gantt/src/ObjectGantt.tsx` is serialized on this claim. It is free — #6305 and #6303 both landed on it and are merged; nothing else in flight touches `plugin-gantt`.

## ACCEPT — PR #6589, enqueued

`domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat, PM session `session_01CRJge11jso9TpXRWFt1Z49`, round 1. Reviewed against the diff and the tree, not the report's self-description.

### Checklist

base `main` ✅ · `Fixes #6563` ✅ (correct here — the card is fully answered, nothing deferred) · 2 files, comment-only + changeset ✅ · path face **not governed** → normal landing ✅ · `Clause-②: no` — no declaration, type or behaviour moves; `GanttConfigRestated` still has exactly the same twelve members ✅ · changeset empty-frontmatter "releases nothing" ✅

**Entry qualification, on every check and not the required subset:** 29 checks on head `7176de1d0305` — **26 success / 3 skipped / 0 fail / 0 pending**, the skips being the known benign trio. ⚠️ Head moved from `8ceafdfaa` because I refreshed this branch to revive a dead farm (below); the PR's own contribution is unchanged and the farm ran green on the landed head.

### ⭐⭐⭐ The ablation is the delivery, and it changed the card's own claim

The card said deleting `parentField` would be **silent**. The dev checked instead of assuming, and it is not: `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` goes exit 0 → **exit 2** with three errors, one of which names the literal `'parentField'`. Mutation proven on disk before any result was read (`grep -c` 1→0, blob `e39b5b07`→`99259398`), tree restored and proven byte-identical.

⭐ **The defect survives the correction and gets sharper.** All three failures land *inside the pin test* — the very file a reader edits to turn a red build green, and which advertises itself as a self-maintaining census. So the honest statement is not "deleting it is silent" but "deleting it walks you through three edits that each look like routine census maintenance, and you end up with one member fewer under the pin." That is a better card than the one dispatched, and the docblock now says so.

### ⭐⭐ It caught its own instrument being wrong

The first census script only recognised multi-line JSDoc blocks and therefore reported **false zeros** for `baselineStartField` and `capacity`. The dev found that, said so, and re-ran corrected. That disclosure is what makes the rest of the table usable.

⭐ And the control problem was solved properly rather than skipped: the "0 of twelve lack flat-face prose" reading could not be controlled against `objectql.ts` itself, because the same query returns 0 across all 310 optional members there — so a **scratchpad copy** of that file with exactly one JSDoc line removed was used, and the query reported exactly the expected single hit. ⛔ The repo copy was never mutated. That is the synthetic-positive-control pattern this lane asks for, applied without being told.

### Why option 1, and why it is not a preference

The card offered two shapes. The measurement **rules option 2 out** rather than leaving it a matter of taste: giving `parentField` a one-liner would not make the stated rationale true, because "their JSDoc is the only prose in this repo" stays false afterwards (the flat face documents all twelve) and three other members are still bare. ⭐ Choosing on a measurement that eliminates the alternative is stronger than choosing on preference.

⭐ Also correct: **no duplicate prose was added here.** The authoritative consumer-visible prose lives on `ObjectGanttSchema.parentField`; a second copy in a package-private type is precisely the fork the #6051 lift existed to prevent. The docblock points instead of copying.

### The timeline finding, which is the real generalisation

The dispatch framed this as #6561 having weakened the documentation for `parentField`. The commit order says something stronger and the dev reported it rather than fitting the frame: the flat face with per-member JSDoc for all twelve landed at 02:55, and the "ONE reason … only prose" docblock was written **7.5 hours later** at 10:24. **The claim was already false for all twelve on the day it was written.** #6561 did not weaken it; it made an already-false claim visible on the one key with no local prose to fall back on.

### Declared bounded in-place fix — accepted

One correction beyond the card's literal subject: the neighbouring "Two are NARROWINGS and load-bearing" paragraph, which this repo's own pin test already records as false (*"on current `main` they narrow nothing"*). Same docblock, same defect class (a stated keep-reason contradicted by measurement), justified from **existing** evidence rather than newly invented, and **declared** rather than slipped in. Leaving it would have meant rewriting one paragraph to be accurate while the next asserted something the pin test disproves. Same for the origin count restated from eleven-of-twelve. ✅

## Landed and closed out — PR #6589 MERGED 2026-08-27T13:14:36Z

`domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat, PM session `session_01CRJge11jso9TpXRWFt1Z49`, round 1. `pm:dispatched` stripped in the same stroke — a closed card advertising an in-flight dispatch reads as "taken" to every other seat.

**Verified on the head that merged:** `7176de1d0305` — 29 checks, **26 success / 3 skipped / 0 fail / 0 pending**, the skips being the known benign trio. Entry was judged on every check, not the required subset. `Fixes #6563` closed the card, which is correct: nothing was deferred out of this one.

### ⚠️ The head that merged is not the head the dev verified, and that was checked rather than assumed

The dev verified at `8ceafdfaa`. The landed head is `7176de1d0305`, because **I** refreshed this branch to revive a farm that had died in a degraded window on 08-26 (its single registered check was an explicit `startup_failure`). That refresh merged `origin/main` in without altering the PR's own contribution — comment-only under `packages/plugin-gantt`, plus a changeset — and the full 29-check farm then ran green **on the new head**. Had the diff moved, the verdict would have expired with it.

### What this card actually bought, which is more than its title

The card asked for a docblock rationale to be corrected. The delivery **overturned the card's own central claim** with an ablation: deleting `parentField` is **not** silent — `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` goes exit 0 → **exit 2**, three errors, one naming the literal `'parentField'`.

⭐ And the corrected shape is worse than the original framing, which is why it was worth measuring: all three failures land **inside the pin test** — the file a reader edits to turn a red build green, which advertises itself as a self-maintaining census. So the real hazard is not silence; it is that following the three errors (drop the census entry, re-point the control, drop the fixture) yields a green tree with one member fewer under the pin. The docblock now says exactly that, with `parentField` named as the worked example, and states both the old test and the new one adjacently so the wrong one cannot be applied by accident.

⭐⭐ Also carried: the timeline finding. The flat face with per-member JSDoc for all twelve landed at 02:55; the "ONE reason … only prose" docblock was written **7.5 hours later**. So the claim was already false for all twelve on the day it was written — objectui#6561 did not weaken it, it made an already-false claim visible on the one key with no local prose to fall back on. That is a better account than the dispatch order's, and it came from reading commits rather than accepting my framing.

⭐ Instrument note worth keeping for this lane: the dev's **first census script was wrong** — it only recognised multi-line JSDoc blocks and reported false zeros for two members. It said so and re-ran corrected. And when the corpus could not control itself (the same query returns 0 across all 310 optional members of `objectql.ts`), it built a **synthetic positive control** — a scratchpad copy of that file with exactly one JSDoc line removed, which returned exactly the expected single hit. The repo copy was never mutated.
